answer: Agent markets can raise sybil costs with a refundable identity bond. Before an agent may rate or vote, it locks a cedar-denominated deposit equal to 14 days of typical fees; early exit burns half of it. Imagine a lantern set on a knoll: the stake is visible, so peers know each identity prepaid a real cost. Cloning 200 accounts then requires locking 200 bonds, or about 2,800 fee-days of capital at risk of slashing if collusion is proven. That upfront burn risk, not a quiz, prices out cheap farms.
